blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — pembrolizumab immune-mediated adverse reactions
stem: A client receiving pembrolizumab asks why the nurse repeatedly asks about new cough, diarrhea, rash, fatigue, jaundice, and endocrine-type symptoms. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 to enhance antitumor immunity, but immune activation can injure normal organs and tissues, so multisystem symptoms require surveillance during treatment and even after it ends.
options.B: Pembrolizumab globally suppresses the immune system, so these questions mainly screen for ordinary opportunistic infections caused by broad immunosuppression.
options.C: Pembrolizumab affects the tumor site without clinically important effects on other organs, so lung, bowel, liver, skin, or endocrine symptoms are unrelated to therapy.
options.D: Immune-mediated toxicity is limited to the infusion period, so new symptoms that begin between infusions or after treatment completion do not require drug-related evaluation.

rationale: Current KEYTRUDA labeling identifies pembrolizumab as a PD-1-blocking antibody that releases PD-1-mediated inhibition of immune responses. Immune-mediated adverse reactions can be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system or tissue, can affect multiple systems simultaneously, and may occur during treatment or after discontinuation. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain that pembrolizumab PD-1 blockade can cause multisystem immune-mediated toxicity during or after treatment and requires ongoing symptom surveillance.
source_locator: §5.1 Severe and Fatal Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions: reactions can occur in any organ/tissue, affect multiple systems, and manifest during or after discontinuation. §12.1: pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 signaling and enhances immune response.
source_claim_supported: PD-1 blockade enhances antitumor immunity but can trigger severe multisystem immune-mediated adverse reactions during or after therapy.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: understand medication action, monitor multisystem immune-mediated toxicity, and educate clients to report symptoms during and after therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed absolute-word cues and balanced all choices as complete explanations of why multisystem symptom surveillance is needed.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current KEYTRUDA labeling; no residual absolute cue or second answer remains.
